title: Fallbrook
status: Cut-to-length launched July 2025; wood door at Gate 0
description:
Fallbrook is CRL's demountable glass partition system for offices. I ran two programs to grow it.

Cut-to-length fabrication. Labor costs are rising and skilled installers are hard to find, so customers wanted partitions that arrive ready to install. We partnered with a fabrication specialist to cut and kit Fallbrook to each opening, and placed the new facility near our Southeast distribution center to serve the East Coast, where most Fallbrook sales are. It launched in July 2025. CRL's European business already sells nearly 80% of its systems this way.

Wood door option. In a partition, the door is usually the weakest point for sound. Two new frame extrusions and floating hinge and strike backup plates let Fallbrook accept standard 1-3/4" U.S. wood doors with the hinges in any position. That suits privacy-critical rooms like law offices, libraries and conference rooms. It passed Gate 0 in March 2026.

brief.label: Problem
brief.text: Rising labor costs and fewer qualified installers meant customers wanted installations that take less time and skill.

brief.label: Solution
brief.text: A cut-to-length fabrication program: Fallbrook components cut and kitted to each opening by a fabrication partner, shipped through our distribution center.

brief.label: Value
brief.text: Installers save time and labor. Temperers get a one-stop shop: material and glass in a box, ready to install in uniquely sized openings.

brief.label: Customers
brief.text: Architects, temperers, glazing contractors and Division 10 contractors.

brief.label: Wood door
brief.text: A kit of two frame extrusions and floating backup plates lets the system accept U.S. standard butt hinges and T, full-lip and ASA strikes anywhere along the jamb.

research_intro: Location data drove the cut-to-length program: where Fallbrook already sells decided where the fabrication partner should build, and the growth trend set the business case.

charts.title: Sound transmission class (STC) for doors
charts.caption: Why a wood door matters: in a partition, the door sets the acoustic ceiling. A solid-core or acoustic wood door with proper seals delivers the biggest privacy gain for the cost.
charts.columns: STC | What can be heard | Glass doors | Wood doors
charts.rows:
25 | Soft speech heard and understood | Single-pane glass | Hollow core
30 | Normal speech heard and understood | Double-glazed glass | Standard lightweight
35 | Loud speech heard and understood | Laminated glass | Solid core
40 | Loud speech heard, not understood | – | Heavy solid core
45 | Loud speech faintly heard | Acoustically insulated glass | –
50 | Shouting faintly heard | – | Acoustic wood
60+ | Soundproofing begins | Specialized glass | –
